description:
LOCATION:
- crate-jmap-contacts-server/Cargo.toml:21-28 (feature declaration)
- crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs:286-328 (demo_next_id)
- crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/lib.rs (no doc-cfg, no API marker)

FEATURE:
    # Switches MemoryBackend::demo_next_id from the default deterministic
    # "<type><n:016x>" pattern to a process-global timestamp+counter
    # pattern matching the canonical jmap-mail-server next_id at
    # email.rs:1748.
    realistic-demo-ids = []

PROBLEM:
This feature changes the runtime behavior of MemoryBackend (the public,
documented reference implementation gated by `feature = "memory"`) but
does not change the API surface at all. Specifically:

1. **No #[doc(cfg(feature = "realistic-demo-ids"))]** anywhere in the
   public docs. Consumers who enable both `memory` and
   `realistic-demo-ids` see the same module docs, the same impl, and
   no rustdoc hint that anything changed.

2. **No compile-time signal.** There is no #[cfg]-gated public item, so
   `--features memory,realistic-demo-ids` produces the same crate
   metadata as `--features memory` would. The only difference is the
   shape of the returned `Id` strings — runtime behavior.

3. **Test breakage risk.** Test fixtures that hardcode expected ids
   (e.g., `assert_eq!(resp["created"]["c1"]["id"], "addressbook0...01")`)
   will pass on default features and fail unpredictably when the
   downstream consumer enables `realistic-demo-ids`. The id format
   under the realistic mode is timestamp-based and not repeatable
   across runs — every test run produces different ids.

4. **Feature unification (Cargo additive features rule).** A downstream
   crate that depends on jmap-contacts-server with default features
   has no way to opt out if some OTHER crate in the dependency graph
   enables `realistic-demo-ids`. Cargo's additive-feature model means
   one transitive enable flips behavior for everyone. The doc comment
   at memory.rs:268-285 calls demo_next_id "NOT A PRODUCTION PATTERN"
   but the production code path is whatever the deepest dependency
   selects.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That the id strings emitted by MemoryBackend are stable across
  feature-flag changes by any dependent crate.
- That `assert_eq!` on observed ids in their test suite continues to
  pass when an unrelated downstream crate enables a feature.

RECOMMENDED:
(a) Move the feature behind a runtime constructor option instead of a
    compile-time feature: `MemoryBackend::new().with_realistic_demo_ids()`.
    Avoids the Cargo feature-unification problem entirely.
(b) If keeping as a cargo feature, add #[doc(cfg(feature = "..."))]
    annotations and ensure the rustdoc renders both modes clearly.
(c) Mark `MemoryBackend::demo_next_id` itself non-public (it already is
    `fn`, not `pub fn`, but mention in the impl-block doc that the
    runtime format is feature-flag-controlled and not part of the
    stability contract).

Filed P2 because the failure mode is observable (test ids change) but
not catastrophic; consumers will discover it via flaky tests rather
than data loss.

PROPAGATION: this feature exists ONLY in contacts-server, not in the
canonical jmap-mail-server (which uses uuid::Uuid::new_v4() directly).
Either remove the feature from contacts-server (and align demo_next_id
with mail-server's uuid approach) or propagate the same feature to the
canonical and the 5 other extension siblings. The current state — a
contacts-only twist on the canonical's id-minting strategy — is a
cookie-cutter regression.
title: realistic-demo-ids feature changes runtime id format with no compile-time signal or API surface marker
